claims.text: Premier's statement on declaration of state of provincial emergency (8 August 2026): BC's Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness, Kelly Greene, declared a State of Provincial Emergency, citing 'the addition of this new, fast-moving fire and the large-scale evacuation that occurred overnight' near Summerland (the Bald Range fire), stating emergency officials 'now need the specific tools it enables available.'

As of 15 August 2026, EmergencyInfoBC lists active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts for the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, City of Revelstoke, Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan Indian Band, Cayoose Creek Indian Band, Village of Clinton and Thompson-Nicola Regional District.

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 17 August 2026): confirms the State of Provincial Emergency declared 8 August 2026 is still in effect, with active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts listed for the Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan Indian Band, Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, District of Summerland, City of Revelstoke and other regional districts and First Nations, most recently updated 16 August 2026.

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 37, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 - 16 Aug 2026): burned area 25,829 hectares (up from 25,391 ha in episode 31); affected population 4,912 people in the burned area (unchanged from episode 31).

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 39, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC - 17 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area 26,618 hectares (up from 25,829 ha in episode 37); affected population 4,912 people in the burned area (unchanged from episode 37).

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 18 August 2026): confirms the State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) remains in effect, with active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts listed across the Cariboo Regional District, Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan-Similkameen, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Fraser Valley Regional District and roughly 25 other affected communities; most recent update dated 17 August 2026 (Cariboo Regional District evacuation information).

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 44, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC - 19 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area 29,128 hectares (up from 26,618 ha in episode 39); affected population 4,912 people in the burned area (unchanged).

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 20 August 2026): the State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) remains in effect, with active wildfire evacuation orders and alerts still listed; no news.gov.bc.ca release announcing an extension or termination of the declaration has been published.

GDACS's wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 49, reporting window 08 August 2026 - 20 August 2026): burned area 29,678 hectares, up from 29,128 hectares in episode 44; affected population unchanged at 4,912 people within the burned area.

GDACS's wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 53, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC - 21 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area 30,182 hectares, up from 29,678 hectares in episode 49; affected population unchanged at 4,912 people within the burned area.

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 22 August 2026): the State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) remains in effect, with active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts still listed, most recently updated for the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen and District of Summerland (21 August 2026) and the Okanagan Indian Band (20 August 2026).

EmergencyInfoBC, provincial State of Provincial Emergency event page (last updated 8 August 2026, 1:00 pm): 'The Province of British Columbia has declared a State of Provincial Emergency due to regional wildfires,' directing residents to BC Wildfire Service and DriveBC for real-time statistics.

Government of British Columbia news release (21 August 2026, 2:04 pm), 'Extending state of emergency due to wildfire risk': the Province 'has extended the state of provincial emergency for a further seven days, until Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026' due to continuing wildfire risk across British Columbia; the release states government 'has not needed to issue emergency orders under the state of emergency to respond to the current wildfire situation,' but is maintaining the declaration so response tools remain available as conditions evolve. The original declaration dates to 8 August 2026.

Government of British Columbia news release (27 August 2026), 'Provincial state of emergency ends, wildfire risk remains': the state of provincial emergency, initially declared 8 August 2026, 'will come to an end on Aug. 27, 2026' following advice from emergency management officials; 'the Province did not need to use those emergency powers.' The release states 'the cancellation of the state of provincial emergency has no effect on current evacuation orders, evacuation alerts or local states of emergencies put in place by local governments or First Nations,' and that 'the Wildfire Act and Emergency and Disaster Management Act continues to provide the Province with the legislative tools currently needed to respond to wildfire emergencies,' with wildfire risk remaining elevated in many parts of the province due to warm, dry conditions.

EmergencyInfoBC's wildfire hazard page lists 19 active local evacuation orders and alerts as of its most recently updated entry (Okanagan Indian Band evacuation information, 4 September 2026), down from the broader set of regional-district evacuation notices tracked in late August; GDACS's wildfire report for the event (id 1030240) remains at its last-recorded figures of 30,182 hectares burned and 4,912 people affected, with no newer episode published since 21 August.
A BC Government News safety advisory for the Labour Day long weekend (issued 3 September 2026, 9:00 AM) states there are currently 160 active wildfires burning in B.C.

EmergencyInfoBC's wildfire hazard page (checked 11 September 2026) lists 14 active local evacuation notices, down from 19 on 4 September: Okanagan Indian Band (updated 9 September), Cariboo Regional District (3 September), Spuzzum First Nation and Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (2 September), Lytton First Nation (31 August), Coldwater Indian Band (29 August), Llenllenéy'ten/High Bar First Nation (28 August), District of Summerland and Ts'kw'aylaxw First Nation (24 August), Boothroyd Indian Band (16 August), Yale First Nation and Shxw'ow'hamel First Nation (1 August), Whispering Pines/Clinton Indian Band (24 July) and Boston Bar First Nation (6 July).

BC Wildfire Service blog post (4 September 2026), 'Area Restriction for Bald Range wildfire rescinded': the Area Restriction Order for the Bald Range wildfire (K51490) near Summerland was rescinded because 'fire behaviour and activity has decreased, firefighting personnel no longer need to restrict public access'; the post notes the site remains an active job site and officials retain authority to order people to leave if conditions change.

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 1): 'Forest fire can have a low humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability.' Burned area: 13,006 hectares. Affected population: 4,746 people in the burned area. Reporting window: 08 Aug 2026 - 11 Aug 2026.

Government of British Columbia news release (10 August 2026, 5:01 pm), 'Supporting Summerland-area evacuees': 'More than 1,000 hotel rooms are available now in the Okanagan for wildfire evacuees,' with nearly 1,000 beds in group lodging throughout the Okanagan, thirteen emergency support services staff and volunteers deployed, a twenty-fold increase in BC Evacuee Helpline staffing capacity, and mobile ServiceBC units deployed to Penticton and Kelowna.

Penticton RCMP statement (9 August 2026): confirms that an 80-year-old Meadow Valley resident 'was attempting to leave her home, along with one member of her family, due to the wildfires when she reportedly died suddenly.' RCMP said they 'believe her death to be a result of the wildfire,' with the BC Coroners Service investigating to confirm the nature of death.

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 12 August 2026, most recent activity dated 11 August 2026): shows an active State of Provincial Emergency and roughly 30 active evacuation-information notices issued by regional districts and First Nations communities, including the Fraser Valley Regional District, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Central and North Okanagan, Cariboo, and Squamish-Lillooet regions.

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 22, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 - 12 Aug 2026): 'Forest fire can have a low humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability.' Burned area: 23,450 hectares (up from 13,006 ha in episode 1). Affected population: 4,911 people in the burned area (up from 4,746).

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 26, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC - 13 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area 24,056 hectares (up from 23,450 ha in episode 22); affected population 4,911 people in the burned area (unchanged from episode 22).

A provincewide state of emergency remains in effect (declared 8 August 2026 by Premier Eby); as of Thursday 13 August 2026, the province had 'more than 1,500 block-booked hotel rooms that are available for evacuees' via renewable weekly Emergency Support Services, after helpline staffing was increased 400% following delays accessing services during peak Summerland-area evacuations.

description: British Columbia declared a state of provincial emergency on 8 August 2026 after the fast-moving Bald Range fire near Summerland forced overnight evacuations, part of a wider wildfire outbreak that killed one person. The province ended the emergency declaration on 27 August, and by early September the Bald Range fire's area restriction had been rescinded as fire activity decreased and active evacuation notices provincewide had eased to 14, though wildfire risk remains elevated with roughly 160 fires still burning as of 3 September.

impact.summary: One death is confirmed: an 80-year-old Meadow Valley resident who died on 9 August 2026 while evacuating from the Bald Range fire near Summerland. GDACS's most recently published figures remain 30,182 hectares burned and 4,912 people affected within the burned area, unchanged since its 21 August 2026 episode. British Columbia ended its province-wide State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) on 27 August 2026, saying it never needed to invoke emergency powers under the declaration. The BC Wildfire Service rescinded the area restriction order for the Bald Range fire itself on 4 September 2026, citing decreased fire behaviour and activity, though the site remains an active job site requiring caution. EmergencyInfoBC's wildfire page lists 14 active local evacuation orders and alerts as of 11 September 2026, down from 19 on 4 September, most recently updated for the Okanagan Indian Band (9 September). Wildfire risk remains elevated province-wide, with a 3 September safety advisory citing 160 wildfires still active across B.C.

location.region: British Columbia Interior, centred on the Bald Range fire near Summerland in the South Okanagan; more than 100 wildfires active provincewide

event.scale: Provincial State of Emergency ended 27 August 2026 (declared 8 August); Bald Range fire (largest, near Summerland) area restriction rescinded 4 September as fire activity decreased; 1 confirmed fatality; 30,182 hectares burned as of 21 August 2026 (GDACS)

name: Wildfire State of Emergency — British Columbia, Canada

updates.text: BC Wildfire Service rescinded the area restriction order for the Bald Range fire on 4 September, citing decreased fire behaviour and activity; EmergencyInfoBC's evacuation-notice count eased to 14 active orders/alerts, down from 19, most recently updated for the Okanagan Indian Band (9 September).
A 3 September BC Government safety advisory put the number of wildfires still active across the province at 160; EmergencyInfoBC's evacuation-order list remained at 19 as of 4 September.

EmergencyInfoBC's wildfire page listed 19 active local evacuation orders and alerts, down from the broader set active across multiple regional districts in late August; GDACS's tracked burned area (30,182 hectares, 4,912 people affected) remains unchanged since 21 August.

British Columbia ended its State of Provincial Emergency on 27 August 2026, two days ahead of its scheduled 29 August expiry, saying it never had to invoke emergency powers under the declaration. The cancellation has no effect on existing wildfire evacuation orders and alerts, still active across multiple regional districts and First Nations; wildfire risk remains elevated province-wide.

British Columbia extended its State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) for a further seven days, to 29 August 2026, citing continuing wildfire risk; the province said it has not needed to issue emergency orders under the declaration to date but is maintaining it so response tools remain available as conditions evolve.

GDACS's episode 53 update, covering to 21 August, put the tracked burned area at 30,182 hectares, up from 29,678, with the affected population unchanged at 4,912; the provincial state of emergency remains in effect with evacuation orders and alerts still active in the Okanagan-Similkameen and Summerland areas.

GDACS's episode 49 update, covering to 20 August, put the tracked burned area at 29,678 hectares, up from 29,128, with the affected population unchanged at 4,912; the provincial state of emergency remains in effect.

GDACS's episode 44 update, covering to 19 August, put the tracked burned area at 29,128 hectares, up from 26,618, with the affected population unchanged at 4,912; the provincial state of emergency remains in effect.
GDACS's episode 39 update, covering to 17 August, put the tracked burned area at 26,618 hectares, up from 25,829, with the affected population unchanged at 4,912.

GDACS's episode 37 update put the tracked burned area at 25,829 hectares, up from 25,391 in episode 31; evacuation orders and alerts remained in force across the North Okanagan, Okanagan-Similkameen, Summerland, Revelstoke and other regional districts and First Nations.
GDACS's episode 31 update recorded 25,391 hectares burned, up from 24,056 in episode 26, with the affected population at 4,912.
The province reported more than 1,500 block-booked hotel rooms available for evacuees, with helpline staffing increased 400% after delays during the peak Summerland-area evacuations.
GDACS's episode 22 update showed the tracked burned area growing to 23,450 hectares from 13,006 in episode 1, with 4,911 people in the burned area.

The province opened more than 1,000 hotel rooms and nearly 1,000 group-lodging beds in the Okanagan for evacuees, deployed mobile ServiceBC units to Penticton and Kelowna, and increased BC Evacuee Helpline staffing capacity twenty-fold.

Penticton RCMP confirmed the outbreak's first fatality: an 80-year-old Meadow Valley resident who died while attempting to evacuate as the Bald Range fire advanced; the BC Coroners Service is investigating.
British Columbia declared a State of Provincial Emergency after the fast-moving Bald Range fire forced a large-scale overnight evacuation near Summerland.
